# Site email

How a site sends its own email (form notifications, the emails to its members): the platform's server when the workspace is allowed it, the site's own SMTP server, or none. The SMTP password is write-only. See the site-email recipe.

[`mail.read`](#mailread) · [`mail.update`](#mailupdate) · [`mail.test`](#mailtest)

## mail.read

Read how the site sends its email: `mode` `platform` (the platform's mail server, allowed only when `platformAllowed`, which the platform admin sets per workspace), `smtp` (the site's own SMTP server, in `smtp` without its password: `hasPassword` says whether one is stored) or `none` (no email leaves: a message to send fails with mail_not_configured, and a form submission is stored with `notification: { status: "failed", error: "mail_not_configured" }`; saving a form with recipients then answers a `form.mail_not_configured` warning finding). `sending` says whether email actually goes out. The site's own mail follows it: form notifications and their tests, and the emails to the site's members; platform account mail (admin password resets, invitations to the admin) always uses the platform's server.

- permission `site.edit` (admin, editor); class `read`; writes nothing.
- Input: `{}`.

Output: { mode: "platform" \| "smtp" \| "none", platformAllowed: boolean, smtp: { host: string (min 1, max 253), port: 25 \| 465 \| 587 \| 2525, security: "starttls" \| "tls", user?: string (min 1, max 320), fromAddress: string (max 320), fromName?: string (min 1, max 80), hasPassword: boolean } \| null, sending: boolean }

Example input:

```json
{}
```

## mail.update

Set how the site sends its email: `mode` `platform`, `smtp` or `none`; with `smtp`, the server as a whole (`host`, a public host name or address, never a local, private or link-local one; `port` 25, 465, 587 or 2525; `security` `starttls` or `tls` (port 465); `user`, null for none; `fromAddress`, which the server must allow; `fromName`). The password is write-only: leave it out or send "" to keep the stored one, null to remove it, a string to replace it; it is stored encrypted and never answered. `platform` is refused with 403 mail_platform_not_allowed unless the workspace may use the platform's server; a refused host is 422 mail_host_refused. The input is redacted from the history and the audit log; not undoable: send the previous settings again. Then run mail.test.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `transaction`; writes `mail`; **not undoable**: alone in its batch.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | "platform" \| "smtp" \| "none" | yes |
| `smtp` | object |  |
| `smtp.host` | string (min 1, max 253) | yes |
| `smtp.port` | 25 \| 465 \| 587 \| 2525 | yes |
| `smtp.security` | "starttls" \| "tls" | yes |
| `smtp.user` | string (min 1, max 320) \| null |  |
| `smtp.fromAddress` | string (max 320) | yes |
| `smtp.fromName` | string (min 1, max 80) |  |
| `smtp.password` | string (max 512) \| null |  |

Output: { mode: "platform" \| "smtp" \| "none", platformAllowed: boolean, smtp: { host: string (min 1, max 253), port: 25 \| 465 \| 587 \| 2525, security: "starttls" \| "tls", user?: string (min 1, max 320), fromAddress: string (max 320), fromName?: string (min 1, max 80), hasPassword: boolean } \| null, sending: boolean }

Example input:

```json
{"mode":"smtp","smtp":{"host":"smtp.example.com","port":587,"security":"starttls","user":"studio@example.com","password":"app-password","fromAddress":"studio@example.com","fromName":"Studio"}}
```

## mail.test

Send a short test email to `to` through the site's mail, as it is now. A failure is answered typed, so you know what to fix: mail_not_configured (the mode is none, or the platform's server is not available to this site), mail_host_refused, mail_auth_failed (user or password), mail_connection_failed (host, port or firewall), mail_tls_failed (the security setting or the certificate), mail_refused (the server took the login but refused the message, often the from address). Run it alone in a batch.

- permission `site.admin` (admin); class `external`; writes nothing; external: alone in its batch, never in a dry run.

| Input | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | yes |

Output: { to: string, mode: "platform" \| "smtp" \| "none", messageId: string }

Example input:

```json
{"to":"studio@example.com"}
```
